exercise.name: Resistance Band Overhead Shoulder Press

reference.title: Resistance Band Overhead Shoulder Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

equipment: Resistance band (two, or one long band under both feet)

breathing.pattern: Brace and breathe out as you press up, breathe in as the hands come back to the shoulders.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.tempo: 2-0-1-1 (2 s down, 1 s up, 1 s at the top)
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower lowering, a wider stance on the band (more stretch), then the next band up.

cues.text: Stand on the bands with the feet a little wider than hip width, knees soft. A band end in each hand at the front of the shoulders, palms forward, elbows under the hands.
Brace, breathe out and press the hands straight up until the arms are straight over the shoulders, the head moving slightly through as the hands pass the face.
Arms straight, biceps beside the ears, ribs down; do not lean back.
Breathe in and bring the hands back to the shoulders under control.
Short pause with the band still taut, then press again.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to finish the press
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down; use a lighter band.
Finish with the hands over the shoulders, not in front of the face.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Start with the elbows slightly forward of the body, under the hands.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bands snap the hands down

kinematics.norm: About 80-90 degrees with the hands at the shoulders to about 165-175 degrees at lockout (clinical opinion)
About 90-110 degrees at the bottom to nearly straight overhead (clinical opinion)
Standing tall without leaning back; standing presses demand more trunk muscle activity than seated ones (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2013).
Each band anchored under the ball of its own foot, so the tension rises toward lockout; elastic resistance can give muscle activity comparable to free weights (Andersen 2010).
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Resistance Band Overhead Shoulder Press, video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Keep the band securely under the ball of each foot; a band that slips out can whip up toward the face.
Shoulder pain overhead: press with the palms facing each other and stop short of full lockout (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: press seated on a bench.
progressions: Stronger band or a wider stance on the band.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover of the press, flexing the shoulder (Campos 2020 compared deltoid portions across shoulder exercises).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover of the press, flexing the shoulder (Campos 2020 compared deltoid portions across shoulder exercises).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Abducts the arm as the elbows travel out and up.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Abducts the arm as the elbows travel out and up.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Rotate the shoulder blades upward and elevate them as the arms go overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Rotate the shoulder blades upward and elevate them as the arms go overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blades upward with the trapezius.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blades upward with the trapezius.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist leaning back as the band tightens.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist leaning back as the band tightens.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk: standing presses load the trunk more than seated ones (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm overhead (clinical opinion).
